acme-cs: Hey team — over the last 20 minutes our ingest pipeline to /v1/embeddings has been getting repeated 504s on batch requests. Happening on eu-west-1 only. Sample request id: req_8a3f2b. Can you look?

elena: Sorry you're hitting this, thanks for flagging. Can you paste the exact curl or SDK call and the batch size?

acme-cs: Using the Node SDK v1.6.2, call looks like: 
```js
client.embeddings.create({ model: 'embed-large-v2', input: [...2000 items...] })
```
We chunk at 2000 inputs, usually fine. This spike started at 13:02 UTC.

ryan_sre: Noted. I see a bunch of 504s from the edge to the inference pool for eu-west-1 around 13:02-13:18 UTC in our traces. Request queue depth jumped and then TCP conn resets.

maya_eng: Could be sustained head-of-line blocking in the batcher when very large combined sequence lengths hit kernel timeouts. Any logs with server side error code?

acme-cs: Edge logs include `upstream read timeout` and the SDK shows a 504. No 5xx body from model host.

aron_support: (typo) -> aaron_support: I'm going to open an internal incident and ask SRE to capture the full pcap and kernel traces. For immediate mitigation, can you try reducing batch size to 256 or enable the SDK incremental batching? Also if you can pass `x-client-request-id: req_8a3f2b` it'll help map.

acme-cs: Trying batch size 256 now. Patch rolled in, will report back in ~5m.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-3478 — assigned to ryan_sre + maya_eng.

ryan_sre: Quick notes from initial capture: connection reuse from client is high (many long-lived HTTP/1.1 keepalives). We're seeing a small subset of requests with very large Content-Length (huge JSON payload), and the inference worker times out after 60s. Edge returns 504. Hypothesis: large payloads + keepalive multiplexing exhausting worker slots.

maya_eng: For repro I ran a local load test with 2000 small texts in a single call and saw worker-side memory spike and significantly increased p99 latency. Setting `max_batch_tokens` and smaller batch sizes avoided the timeout. We'll push a temp fallback that rejects >5120 tokens per request with a 429 to prevent queue storm.

acme-cs: Reducing batch to 256 fixed the immediate 504s for our traffic. Thanks. We'll update the client to chunk smaller.

aaron_support: Customer comms draft: "We're seeing increased timeouts in eu-west-1 for very large embedding batches. Immediate fix: reduce batch size to <=256 or enable incremental batching. We're rolling a platform-side guard to block oversized requests temporarily and will follow up with a permanent scaling fix." Thoughts?

ryan_sre: LGTM. We'll also enable a short-term routing fallback to eu-central for affected tenants while we tune autoscaling thresholds.

maya_eng: Action items: (1) deploy guard (reject >5120 tokens) — PR in flight, (2) tune batcher kernel timeout thresholds, (3) add client-side example in KB for chunking in SDK.

acme-cs: Appreciated. Please keep us posted about the fallback and long-term fix. Ticket INC-2026-3478 is fine.

elena: I'll update the customer in 15m with mitigation steps and the temporary workaround. Closing loop after postmortem. :thumbsup:
